bld_note: Modelled (SFINCS 20 m), uncalibrated. Not a forecast.
hex_note: A screening rank: people affected × how often it floods. It says where to look first, not where to act.
d_warn_title: This is not a warning system
d_warn: This map is a non-commercial research demo. For official alerts, see IGEBU and Burundi's civil protection. Do not use these numbers to decide on an evacuation.
d_what: Three simulated storms from the SFINCS model at 20 m: maximum water depth, affected buildings and an estimate of the people involved. The model has not been calibrated on a real flood, and it floods too much.
d_ev_cop: Against the Copernicus EMSN191 model (scenario 4, the same conditions as scenario 3): CSI {csi}, hit rate {hit}, false-alarm ratio {far}. It finds almost everything Copernicus floods, but floods about 40% more area ({model} km² against {ref} km²).
d_ev_gfm: Against Sentinel-1 in 2024: the satellite saw only {obs} km² of flooding against {model} km² modelled. 2024 was mostly a lake rise, so this test does not measure storm-flood quality.
d_ev_sur: The fast machine-learning preview (next phase) reproduces SFINCS with a CSI of {s0} to {s1} on unseen storms and {c0} to {c1} on an unseen catchment.
d_datum: The lake level is 772.50 m (EGM2008, the 2024 peak). A press figure of about 777 m is a local gauge reading: do not mix the two.
d_people: People come from WorldPop 2020, shared among buildings by floor area. The estimate can be wrong in informal areas. Counts are rounded and shown only per area, never per building. Neighbourhoods are cells around 77 points, not official boundaries.
d_lake: Lake Tanganyika is excluded from areas and colours: the model shows about 2.5 m of water there, which is open water, not flooding.
d_s1_note: Scenario 1 predates a model fix (curve numbers); the measured effect on the other scenarios is under 1%.
